topic: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT): From Chaos to Order

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Normal Distribution
lecture_lines: It is often called the Bell Curve.
Many phenomena follow this predictable pattern.
animations: Display normal curve #FFFFFF, label it 'Normal Dist' #FF0000. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bell.svg]
Show data points clustered near the center. #FFFFFF

sections.title: The Problem: What if the Source is Non-Normal?
lecture_lines: What if the source is not normal?
How do sample means behave then?
animations: Show failure of normal distribution assumptions. #FF0000
Transition to a question mark symbol #FFFFFF [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].

sections.title: The Central Limit Theorem Unveiled
lecture_lines: The CLT is a fundamental statistical theorem.
Sample means approach normal distribution as n grows.
This holds regardless of the initial shape.
It turns chaos into orderly patterns.
animations: Show multiple random samples from skewed population [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/population.svg] #0088FF.
Observe sample means forming a normal curve #FF0000.
Highlight the convergence as sample size increases. #FFFF00

sections.title: Critical Constraints: The 'Magic' Number
lecture_lines: A sample size of 30 is sufficient.
This makes the Bell curve narrower.
animations: Show distribution with n=5 being non-normal #FF8800.
Show distribution with n=35 being normal [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bell.svg] #00FF00.

sections.title: Why This Matters: Real-World Power
lecture_lines: We can use it for hypothesis testing.
It builds a bridge to reliable data.
animations: Show CLT enabling inference on non-normal populations #FFFFFF.
